title: Fields of a padded quadruple
statement: Let $\alpha$, $x$, and $w$ be bit strings, and let $n,t\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose the length of $w$ is one more than the length of the encoding $\langle\alpha,x,1^n,1^t\rangle$, where $1^k$ denotes the word of $k$ ones. Append $w$ to this encoding to form $z$. Then $z$ satisfies the validity guard; its code field is $\alpha$, its input field is $x$, its width and clock fields have lengths $n$ and $t$, respectively, and its certificate part is $w$.
hypotheses_covered: The length of $w$ is the length of $\langle\alpha,x,1^n,1^t\rangle$ plus one
replaced: Let $\alpha, x, w$ be bit strings and $n, t \in \mathbb{N}$, let $y = \langle\alpha,\langle x,\langle 1^n,1^t\rangle\rangle\rangle$ ($1^k$ the word of $k$ ones), suppose $|w| = |y| + 1$, and let $z = yw$. Write $s(z)$ for its odd split (the self-delimiting pair encoding $\langle z_{[:i]}, z_{[i:]}\rangle$ when $|z| = 2i+1$, and the empty word when $|z|$ is even), $\pi_1, \pi_2$ for the two components of a pair encoding (the empty word when parsing fails), $Y = \pi_1(s(z))$ and $W = \pi_2(s(z))$; the code, input, width and clock fields of $z$ are $\pi_1(Y)$, $\pi_1(\pi_2(Y))$, $\pi_1(\pi_2(\pi_2(Y)))$ and $\pi_2(\pi_2(\pi_2(Y)))$. The guard $G(z)$ holds when $s(z)$, $Y$, $\pi_2(Y)$ and $\pi_2(\pi_2(Y))$ all parse as pair encodings and the width and clock fields consist only of ones. Then $G(z)$ holds, the code field of $z$ is $\alpha$, its input field is $x$, its width and clock fields have lengths $n$ and $t$, and $W = w$.
